research.title: CAT Initiation: Power Story or Cycle Stock?
research.summary: Accumulate on weakness at $558.63: build below about $530 and add toward $480. The 2026 sell-off was a multiple reset, not an earnings miss, and the power backlog is sold out into 2029-30. About four-fifths of sales are still cyclical, so fair value is capped near 19x 2027 earnings.

research.title: AI infrastructure, the next 12 months: re-evaluating the AI hardware basket
research.summary: The midterms raised the odds of a slower, more constrained US data-center build-out. AI demand stays strong, so the call is selective growth: prefer TSM and AMD, do not add to NVDA, sell LITE, keep COHR small, and hold BE.

research.title: Earnings update Q3 2026: Amazon, Meta, Shopify
research.summary: Amazon is open to outside agents on its own terms, Meta's Muse works but the bill arrived as negative free cash flow and a $95bn raise, and Shopify's rail held while the stock fell. Visa says agent volume is still too small to matter in 2027.

research.title: Binance heist: what it means for our cyber basket
research.summary: The largest crypto theft on record ran through a poisoned package, a fake job offer, an over-privileged token and an internal AI tool. No change to the basket, but it points to identity and software supply chain. A fear-driven slowdown in AI agents helps the basket. A return-driven one is the real risk.

research.title: Channel check: what a Nobel Prize-winning mRNA lab at Penn told us about AI, monkeys and the wet lab
research.summary: A Penn mRNA scientist confirmed that monkeys, wet-lab capacity and labour are the scarce inputs in drug discovery, and flagged two risks: AI still needs heavy human checking, and China is now the cheapest source of lab kit.

research.title: Cybersecurity hardware: Fortinet and F5
research.summary: Both names fell about 20% on earnings in the same week. The moat is being physically in the data path inside the customer's building, which AI cannot vibe-code. Own the category at equal weight, but wait: the entry conditions and kill triggers are set out name by name.

research.title: If frontier AI labs are becoming the next generation of biotech platforms, how should we position?
research.summary: Frontier AI labs are buying biotechs, building wet labs and starting their own drug programmes. Design gets cheap and validation stays scarce, so the physical layer gets paid: molecule makers, lab tools, testing services and data owners.

research.title: Update on the cybersecurity basket: six new names
research.summary: Five weeks in, the nine-name basket is up 11.4% against 6.0% for IGV. We map security spend into eight layers, ask where AI agents push growth fastest, and add six names: MSFT, FROG, QLYS, ACN, CACI and MITK.

research.title: The Mall Is Closing: Shopify, Meta's Muse and the Agentic Storefront
research.summary: When AI agents do the shopping, the rails get paid every time (Shopify), the assistant that knows the buyer earns a commission (Meta), and the everything store has to reinvent itself or shrink (Amazon).

research.title: Passport Control for Robots: SAIL vs OKTA
research.summary: AI agents pay the identity registry, not the login. Governance is priced per identity, login per employee. Within listed identity, SailPoint owns the better-placed layer at the lower multiple.

research.title: AI agentic beneficiaries: cybersecurity theme primer and shopping list
research.summary: Who gets paid when software starts doing the work: the traffic, the control points and the record-keeping that every AI agent has to pass through. A shopping list, built before the down day we cannot time.

research.title: The USD Debasement Basket: initiation report
research.summary: Gold royalty and streaming companies are the hedge we need for the financial repression era. Basket: FNV, WPM, AEM and ALS.
